title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 3 (Ablation study on ScanRefer), row 'w/o L_div'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The table reports RSum = 191.7 for the 'w/o L_div' ablation with R@1=35.1, R@5=69.4, R@10=84.1. But 35.1 + 69.4 + 84.1 = 188.6, not 191.7 (off by +3.1). All other rows in Table 3 (Full IDeal, w/o Q1, w/o Q2, w/o p̂1, w/o p̂2, w/o p̂3, w/o CoT, w/o IAT, w/o L_dis) are internally consistent: RSum exactly equals R@1+R@5+R@10. This is a provable arithmetic error in the reported headline metric.

The constraint written as 'u_i^j o_i^T <= R_i, for all j' defines a half-space (a linear inequality on a hyperplane), NOT a hypersphere/ball. A minimum enclosing hypersphere (as in the cited SVDD, Tax & Duin 2004) requires a squared-norm constraint '||u_i^j - o_i||^2 <= R_i^2'. The printed formulation also mixes a raw dot product between two feature vectors with the radius, which is dimensionally inconsistent with a ball enclosing the features. The equation does not describe the claimed minimum enclosing hypersphere.

The text cites '[44, 60]' for a 'structural density bias' and defines '[60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022.' However (a) the reference list ends at [59], so entry [60] does not exist in the bibliography, and (b) targeted web searches for 'Bayesian Density Correction Cross-Modal Retrieval ICLR 2022' and related phrasings return no such paper in the scientific record. The citation appears to be fabricated and is at minimum an internal reference-list inconsistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 vs Table 1, RoMa baseline row (ScanRefer)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In Table 1, RoMa (coarse-grained, non-†) on ScanRefer is 11.4 / 34.8 / 54.4 / 100.6. In Table 2 the RoMa baseline row on ScanRefer is 9.7 / 33.1 / 50.2 / 93.0 — which is EXACTLY the VSE∞ row in both tables. The same baseline model (RoMa) cannot have two different ScanRefer results across the two tables; Table 2's RoMa row is a copy-paste of VSE∞. (Table 2's RoMa Nr3D numbers also differ from Table 1's RoMa Nr3D: 8.3/27.9/37.2/73.4 vs 6.5/24.8/37.6/68.9.)

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2.1, Density Compensated Factor rho(v_i) and corrected similarity
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines rho(v_i) = 1 / ((1/k) * sum_{j in N_k(v_i)} D(v_i, v_j) + epsilon), then sets S̃ = S * sqrt(rho(v_j)), and states 'This formulation ensures that high-density regions receive appropriately reduced similarity scores.' But in a high-density region the average k-NN distance is small, so rho is LARGE, and multiplying S by sqrt(rho) INCREASES the similarity score in high-density regions — the exact opposite of the stated bias-mitigation objective. Either the reciprocal should be inverted or the corrected similarity should divide by sqrt(rho); the formula and the prose are mutually contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2.2, feature-level fusion for Q1 responses
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The weighted linear fusion is written as 'u_i^j = alpha * u_i^j + (1 - alpha) * u_i^{j-1}, where q_i^j in Q1'. The variable u_i^j appears on BOTH sides, making the equation self-referential: solving it (alpha != 1) yields u_i^j = u_i^{j-1}, i.e., the 'fused' feature is identical to the previous round, contradicting the stated goal of preserving core cues while emphasizing newly introduced details. The right-hand side's u_i^j should denote the new response feature, which is a different quantity from the fused left-hand side — a notational/definitional error that makes the equation collapse to a tautology.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.3, Equation (9), weighted complementary contrastive loss L_div
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: L_div contains the term sum_{i} sum_{j!=i} exp(-max(0, S(ũ_i,ũ_j)-gamma)) * log(1 - S(ũ_i,ũ_j)). For a negative pair the objective should push similarity DOWN, i.e. minimize -log(1-S) (binary cross-entropy form, which goes to +inf as S→1). As printed, the term is +log(1-S), whose derivative w.r.t. S is -1/(1-S) < 0, so minimizing it drives S toward 1 — attracting the negative pair. The text states the term 'optimizes the expectation over negative pairs' under divergence-risk minimization, which requires the opposite direction; the missing negative sign reverses the loss's gradient.

The Abstract claims IDeal 'completely solves the alignment challenge between texts and 3D scenes through continuous interaction, achieving near-perfect retrieval accuracy across diverse query types.' However, the best reported R@1 in Table 1 is 37.8 (ScanRefer), 26.4 (Nr3D), and 20.2 (Sr3D), and the paper's own Limitations section states 'First, the performance of the methods is relatively low.' 'Near-perfect retrieval accuracy' is in direct tension with R@1 values in the 20-38% range and the authors' own admission of low absolute performance.

The paragraph contains a duplicated/truncated sentence fragment: 'We begin by integrating information and descriptions of the same scenes from the training data to construct simulated memory for text augmentation. Following IRR, we first provide a training-data-based answerer (i.e., an LLM) with the constructed memory and initial queries. We then simulate the' followed by a blank line and 'We simulate the IRR interaction process by iteratively posing a fixed number of Q1 and Q2 questions.' The 'We then simulate the' fragment is left incomplete and the sentence is restarted, indicating an editing artifact that interrupts the methodology description.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification (threshold 0.30, strictness lenient) of IDeal found 9 issues, several of which are erratum-worthy. The strongest is a provable arithmetic error in Table 3: the 'w/o L_div' row reports RSum 191.7 when R@1+R@5+R@10 = 35.1+69.4+84.1 = 188.6 (confidence 0.9). Two other high-confidence findings: (a) the inline citation [60] 'Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval' (ICLR 2022) is absent from the reference list (which ends at [59]) and could not be found in the literature via web search, indicating a fabricated reference; and (b) Equation (4)'s constraint 'u_i^j o_i^T <= R_i' defines a half-space, not the claimed minimum enclosing hypersphere (SVDD requires ||u_i^j - o_i||^2 <= R_i^2). Table 2's RoMa row is a copy-paste of VSE∞'s ScanRefer numbers (9.7/33.1/50.2/93.0) contradicting Table 1's RoMa (11.4/34.8/54.4/100.6). The Density Compensated Factor formula has the inverse direction of its stated objective (multiplying by sqrt(rho) boosts, not reduces, high-density similarity). The Q1 fusion equation u_i^j = alpha*u_i^j + (1-alpha)*u_i^{j-1} is self-referential and collapses to u_i^j = u_i^{j-1}. Equation (9)'s +log(1-S) term has the wrong sign to repel negatives. Moderate concerns: the Abstract's 'near-perfect retrieval accuracy' contradicts the results (best R@1 37.8/26.4/20.2) and the Conclusion's admission that 'the performance of the methods is relatively low'; a duplicated sentence fragment in Section 3.3. Tables 1-3 RSum arithmetic was otherwise checked and consistent.
